title: Fractera Auth — sign-in for every element of your node
description: One service tells every element who came and with which roles. Email and password work from the start, guests come on demand, and the accounts stay on your own computer.

blocks.title: Sign-in for every element of your node
blocks.description: One service tells every element who came and with which roles. Email and password work from the start, guests come on demand, and the accounts stay on your own computer.

blocks.text: An element sends the visitor’s cookie to /api/session and gets the session with its roles, or 401.
Email and password from the start; Google and a Resend magic link open as soon as their keys are in.
Fourteen roles and the guest, and every route of an element says who may open it.
An element on its own domain
It signs people in through the single sign-on: a one-time code becomes a ticket of that site.
The first account registered on this computer becomes the architect of the node for good.

head: Without it
With the sign-in service
rows: Every element would build its own sign-in
Every element asks one service who came
A visitor’s half-filled cart is lost
A guest account keeps what a visitor did in this browser
Roles are copied by hand into every app
Fourteen roles and the guest, set for every route
The accounts sit on someone else’s server
They stay in one file on your computer, never in git

items: On this computer, register the first account: it becomes the architect of the node.
Connect your own domain: on the temporary address sign-in and registration are closed.
Add a Google or a Resend key when you want those ways in; email and password need nothing.

blocks.text: Every account of the node is seen and changed in the core, on the Users tab of this element. Deleting an account wipes the personal data and keeps the identifier and the journal.
An element of the node asks the service with the visitor’s cookie:
Guests come on demand and stay bounded: a limit per address, and a ceiling on guest records, where the guest inactive the longest leaves first.

Who came and with which roles, or 401

Single sign-on for an element on its own domain
82 languages
Every sign-in screen speaks the visitor’s language, built into the page
Applications
On an app factory each application has its own people: one email in two applications is two accounts

blocks.text: Change sign-in early in the life of your application: it carries the highest risk. If sign-in breaks, nobody opens the protected routes, the architects included, and it is restored through the development mode.

Built by Fractera for the [Lagrix](https://lagrix.dev) protocol and for any web2 project that needs sign-in. MIT license, the code is at [github.com/Fractera/fractera-auth-starter](https://github.com/Fractera/fractera-auth-starter).
